ns2:section.sectionText: "The Molecular Me: An Investigation of Self" As researchers continue to identify important genetic factors in many diseases and conditions, conversations about genetic testing have grown. Acquiring personal genetic data is affordable and offers information about one?s ancestry, traits, and disease risks ? but also opens up new questions. There is a growing need for education on how to interpret the data and the benefits and risks of acquiring this information. This course will provide valuable information about the analytical chemistry of the method, the reliability of the analysis, and the use of various resources to interpret one?s own data. Students registered for this course will be given the option to research their own genetic data acquired via an established "direct-to-consumer" genotyping service. Class will meet in room 2369 Beckman.
